title: Meet System
description: Build a structure with NumPy, JAX, or Torch. Explore positions, atomic types, and the periodic cell.
objective: Construct a System with NumPy, Torch or JAX; explain what the object owns and what an energy model must supply.

title: Metadata & pair lists
description: Describe quantities and capabilities, attach pair lists, and inspect custom data.
objective: Describe model outputs and attach a labeled pair list without confusing metadata with execution.

title: NumPy model
description: Explore a harmonic pair potential with analytic energy, forces, and stress.
objective: Derive and evaluate energy, forces and configurational stress for a harmonic pair.

title: JAX derivatives
description: Differentiate a System pytree. Compare force and stress formulas with explicit strain derivatives.
objective: Differentiate a core System pytree and verify stress through an independent homogeneous deformation.

title: Torch autograd
description: Start an autograd graph from System arrays and compare eager and compiled tensor kernels.
objective: Place the autograd boundary correctly and verify energy, forces and stress before and after graph capture.

title: Relaxation engine
description: Follow fixed-cell relaxation through a linked energy map, structures, and force arrows.
objective: Implement force-driven relaxation and distinguish convergence from reaching the iteration limit.

title: Differentiable pair lists
description: Build a periodic ASE neighbor list, attach core pair data, and differentiate a pair kernel.
objective: Build periodic pair topology and reconstruct vectors inside a differentiable kernel.

title: Outputs & model contract
description: Label energy gradients, serialize predictions, and inspect which model APIs are available.
objective: Encode energies and their derivatives with correct labels, signs and units, then recover them after serialization.

title: ASE dynamics · 3 backends
description: Write an ASE calculator around core System and run NVE dynamics with NumPy, JAX, or Torch.
objective: Connect three evaluators to an ASE calculator and diagnose integration error using total energy.

title: Batching & profiling
description: Batch JAX predictions, check Torch parity, time synchronized calls, and inspect profiler events.
objective: Separate batch correctness, compilation, synchronized timing and profiler interpretation.

title: API progress & prototypes
description: Track every Python API todo, exercise errors and JSON, and explore model, loader, and engine prototypes.
objective: Audit implemented Python primitives and assess model/loader prototypes against the accepted C++ contract.

title: LAMMPS: forces and virial
description: Convert configurational stress to virial; specify pair, fix, compute and MPI responsibilities.

title: GROMACS: unit conversion
description: Derive energy, force and stress conversion factors; verify virtual-work invariance.

title: PLUMED: bias force chain rule
description: Differentiate a distance restraint, then check the bias forces against finite differences.

title: ASE: calculator state
description: Exercise cached results and geometry invalidation; specify the core calculator boundary.

title: i-PI: atomic units and virial
description: Convert energy, forces and virial to atomic units and verify the round trip.

title: Chemiscope: property targets
description: Build structure and atom properties with units, force arrows and copied geometry.

title: TorchSim: packed geometry
description: Reduce per-atom energies by system and expose row/column cell conventions with a skew cell.

title: Native LJ: load and execute
description: Inspect the accepted C++ plugin, satisfy pair requests, and turn energy gradients into forces.

title: NumPy LJ: analytic derivatives
description: Write an energy-shifted LJ kernel, check derivatives, and compare labeled native outputs.

title: Torch LJ: eager and compiled
description: Author an nn.Module, verify compiled values and gradients, then check native parity.

title: C++ LJ contract & parity
description: Execute the upstream C++ LJ plugin and compare NumPy, Torch and JAX outputs, gradients and selection semantics.
objective: Execute the accepted C++ LJ plugin and compare values, gradients and labels with three Python kernels.
